name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,342

clue.text: I'm suffering with distemper over old PM

indicators.note: something suffering is in a bad way, so the letters are knocked out of their order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
O is the standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: An ailing pet with distemper is laid on top of an elderly prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: PM looks like a prime minister but is the clock abbreviation, written out in full as the Latin POST MERIDIEM.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviation for afternoon times stands for the Latin phrase meaning after midday.

clue.text: Tablet screens held up behind hidden danger

indicators.note: to screen something is to shield it from view, so one word wraps around the other
in a down clue, lifting a word up makes it read from bottom to top

blocks.note: a tablet of medicine is a pill
aft means at the back, especially of a ship

explanation.surface: A tablet computer is propped up to hide some lurking hazard.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitfall is a concealed trap or unsuspected difficulty, literally a covered pit.

clue.text: Ross, perhaps, cut disc for head of Motown?

definitions.note: an example: the question mark admits any boss would do

indicators.note: cutting something short trims off its final letter

blocks.note: Diana Ross sang with the Supremes, so she was a Supreme
the letter O is disc-shaped

explanation.surface: Diana Ross trimming a record to suit the boss of her Motown label.
explanation.walkthrough: The Supremes were Diana Ross's Motown girl group.
explanation.definitionFit: A supremo is the person in overall charge of an organisation, such as a record label.

clue.text: Criminal races off to break into Polo?

indicators.note: off here means gone wrong, so the letters are spoilt into a new order
breaking into something puts one thing inside another

blocks.note: taken as written
a Polo is a British mint sweet with a hole in the middle

explanation.surface: A villain dashes off to burgle a polo club, or a game of polo.
explanation.walkthrough: Polo looks like the sport or the car, but the question mark points to the Polo mint, a ring-shaped British sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: A miscreant is a wrongdoer or villain, used as a noun just as criminal can be.

clue.text: Eddy sees old queen going both ways over time

indicators.note: a thing going both ways appears once forwards and once backwards, either side of the middle

blocks.note: R for Regina, queen, with O for old, read in one direction
T is the standard abbreviation for time
the same pair read in the other direction

explanation.surface: Someone named Eddy watches an elderly queen walking up and down for a long while.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer reads the same in both directions, with the time in the centre.
explanation.definitionFit: In meteorology a rotor is a rotating eddy of air, often forming in the lee of mountains.

clue.text: Conflict can be hell with my daughter

blocks.note: Dis is the Roman underworld
cor is a British exclamation of surprise like 'my!'
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A parent laments that rows with their daughter can be hellish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' is the exclamation, not the possessive; COR is the British equivalent.
explanation.definitionFit: Discord is strife or disagreement between people, the same state as conflict.

clue.text: Letter bomb with note has street cordoned off

indicators.note: an area cordoned off is surrounded by a barrier, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: E is a musical note
to cost a bomb is to cost a pile, a large sum of money
ST is the standard abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: A letter bomb is found and police tape off the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter bomb' reads as one item, but the definition stops at Letter; bomb means a fortune, as in 'cost a bomb'.
explanation.definitionFit: An epistle is a formal or literary letter, like those of the New Testament apostles.

clue.text: Rocky point in coast that prevents evacuation?

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for a noun

indicators.note: something rocky is unsteady and shaken up, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A rocky headland on the coast that blocks people from being evacuated.
explanation.walkthrough: Evacuation suggests getting people out of danger; here it is the bodily sense of emptying the bowels.
explanation.definitionFit: Constipation is a condition in which bowel movements are blocked or difficult.

clue.text: Seafood and duck starters in carvery totally work

indicators.note: starters are what come first, so only the opening letters are kept

blocks.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, shaped like O
the first letters of these two words
an opus is a creative work

explanation.surface: A menu of fish dishes, roast duck and carvery starters all keeping a cook busy.
explanation.definitionFit: Octopus is eaten as seafood in many cuisines, grilled or stewed.

clue.text: Some protest if you bear witness to the Lord

indicators.note: only some of the following words is used, a run of letters inside them

blocks.note: the letters run across these words

explanation.surface: A preacher urges that if you object, you should declare your faith publicly.
explanation.definitionFit: In evangelical usage to testify is to declare one's faith publicly, giving witness for God.

clue.text: By and large, no prep’s needed for that vegetable

indicators.note: preparation in a kitchen means chopping and reworking, so these letters are reorganised

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook remarks that this particular vegetable mostly needs no preparation.
explanation.definitionFit: The yard-long bean is an Asian legume with very long edible pods, eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Animal brand clothing Bill shortened

indicators.note: clothing something covers it all round, so one word wraps the other
shortening a word lops off its final letter

blocks.note: to brand is to sear with a hot iron
a bird's bill is its beak

explanation.surface: A fashion label for animal-themed clothing is run by a man named Bill who has been cut down.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill looks like a name or an invoice; it is a bird's beak.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea bear is an old name for the polar bear and also for the fur seal, both animals.

clue.text: Head of office interfering with work schedule - cock

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
something interfering with another gets right inside it

blocks.note: the opening letter of this word
a roster is a rota of duties

explanation.surface: An office manager meddles with the staff rota, and someone calls it a cock-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A rooster is the North American name for a cock, the adult male chicken.

clue.text: Good place to go with one in White House?

definitions.note: a cryptic description: a house made of white snow

blocks.note: Roman numeral one
G is the standard abbreviation for good
loo is British slang for a toilet

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the White House has a decent toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: White House suggests the president's residence; here it is any house that is white, made of snow.
explanation.definitionFit: An igloo is a dome-shaped Inuit shelter built of snow blocks, so literally a white dwelling.

clue.text: Very much what a poker player hopes for?

definitions.text: what a poker player hopes for?

blocks.note: first meaning: to a great extent

blocks.clueFragment: what a poker player hopes for?
blocks.note: second meaning: a favourable set of cards dealt

explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads the phrase literally: a deal of cards that is good.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a large amount, and literally describes a strong hand handed out by the dealer.

clue.text: Men right to defend box with a load of players

indicators.note: defenders stand around what they protect, so the outer letters surround the next word

blocks.note: OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
R is the standard abbreviation for right
a chest is a large box
taken as written

explanation.surface: Soldiers rightly guard a box beside a large group of performers.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestra is a large ensemble of instrumental musicians playing together.

clue.text: Gold in those days mostly beat sterling

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
then means at that time
a tick is a single beat of a clock

explanation.surface: Back in the day, gold nearly always outdid the British pound.
explanation.walkthrough: Sterling looks like the British currency, which fits beside gold; here it is the adjective meaning genuine.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterling as an adjective means of true worth and genuine quality, as in sterling silver.

clue.text: Type of model briefly annoyed with small tops

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: the Model T was Ford's famous car
shirty is British slang for irritable
S is the standard abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A fashion model gets briefly cross at being given undersized tops.
explanation.definitionFit: T-shirts are casual short-sleeved upper garments, a kind of top.

clue.text: Moderate FA fines after drugs report?

indicators.note: a report is something spoken and heard, so the answer is the sound of a phrase

blocks.note: once the football body hands out fines, the Es (ecstasy tablets) are off

explanation.surface: A news story about the Football Association fining players after a drugs scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: E is slang for an ecstasy tablet; the FA is the Football Association, English football's governing body.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease off is to reduce intensity or slacken, which is what moderate means as a verb.

clue.text: Work hard investigating where two grand's gone?

indicators.note: grand is a thousand, written as a single letter, and two of them have gone missing

blocks.note: digging into something is investigating it
G is short for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: Someone works hard tracing where two thousand pounds disappeared to.
explanation.definitionFit: To dig in is to apply oneself with determination and effort, like getting stuck into a task.

clue.text: Agree to get up around about morning - yeah, right!

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means reading the word from the bottom upward
going around something encloses it

blocks.note: to nod is to show agreement
re means concerning or about
AM is the abbreviation for morning hours

explanation.surface: Someone agrees to get out of bed early in the morning, and a sceptic scoffs.
explanation.definitionFit: Dream on is a sarcastic retort meaning that what someone hopes for will never happen.

clue.text: Leave a boxing match or circulate

blocks.note: to go is to leave
taken as written
a bout is a contest in boxing

explanation.surface: A choice between walking out of a fight or mingling with the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: To go about is to move around from place to place, as a rumour or person circulates.

clue.text: Current husband to blow wife away quickly

indicators.note: sending something away removes it from the word

blocks.note: in means fashionable or current
H is the standard abbreviation for husband
to blow money is to waste it
W is the standard abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A present husband hurries to get rid of his wife.
explanation.definitionFit: In haste is an adverbial phrase meaning hurriedly, the same sense as quickly.

clue.text: Result of sex being banned from bathroom?

indicators.note: something banned from a place is kept out of it, so those letters are removed

blocks.note: it is a coy word for sex
an en suite is a bathroom attached to a bedroom

explanation.surface: A newspaper asks what happens when sex is forbidden in the bathroom.
explanation.walkthrough: Result reads as a noun but works as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to follow as a consequence, exactly what to result means as a verb.

clue.text: Animal we blame after letting rip?

indicators.note: letting rip means letting loose wildly, so the letters fly about into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone breaks wind and, as usual, everyone blames the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewe lamb is a young female sheep, a farm animal.

clue.text: New series on artist going around southern waterways

indicators.note: going around means turning back, so the word runs in the opposite direction
in an across clue, one thing on another comes after it, so the series follows the artist

blocks.note: N is the standard abbreviation for new
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
a row is a series of things in a line
S is the standard abbreviation for southern

explanation.surface: A painter tours the canals of the south for a new series of works.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrows are narrow stretches of water such as straits, linking larger bodies of water.

clue.text: Lottery money turns around heart of Humber area

indicators.note: turning something round makes it face the other way
the heart of a word is its middle
going around something encloses it

blocks.note: loot is slang for money
the two central letters of this word
A is the standard abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: Lottery cash circulates around the centre of the Humber region.
explanation.walkthrough: The Humber is an estuary in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A tombola is a lottery at a fete, where tickets are drawn from a revolving drum.

clue.text: A Stones fan rocks out on vacation quite frequently

indicators.note: something on vacation is emptied of its contents, leaving only the outside letters
rocking shakes things about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
just the first and last letters of this word

explanation.surface: A Rolling Stones fan regularly rocks out while away on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: Vacation sounds like a holiday; here it means emptying, so the middle of the word is cleared out.
explanation.definitionFit: As often as not is an idiom meaning about half the time, which is quite frequently.
